newsitem.title: USA: N.Y.C. gets $260 mln of retail orders for Wed sale.
newsitem.headline: N.Y.C. gets $260 mln of retail orders for Wed sale.

text.p: New York City on Tuesday said it had sold approximately $260 million of new bonds to individual investors during the presale period, one of the largest amounts in the past 10 or so such deals.

Late orders pushed Monday's total of around $140 million up to $170 million, while the city got another $90 million of orders this afternoon, before the presale period ended, said a New York City official, who declined to be named.
New York City on Wednesday will sell nearly $1 billion of debt in an offering that includes $172 million of issues for which overseas investors can compete.

A rough target for retail sales was around $200 million, the city official said. He noted a third maturity was closed, the year 2002, after the 2000 and 2001 maturities sold out on Friday, when the retail presale period began.
Retail investors, who typically prefer intermediate maturities, also displayed interest in the long-end.

"We have some strong orders further out the maturity scale than we normally do," the city official said. "That's going to support tomorrow's deal very nicely." From $5 to $10 million of orders was placed for the 2008-2009 maturities.
